mainTopic: The battle with the יצר הרע, end-of-days figures in the נביאים, and the lighting at שמחת בית השואבה.
overview: This amud continues the אגדה about the יצר הרע. ריש לקיש teaches that it attacks a person every day, and only הקדוש ברוך הוא's help lets him win. דבי רבי ישמעאל says to drag it into the בית המדרש, because תורה wears it down like water on stone or smashes it like a hammer. Other teachings show how it grows: it tempts a person and later testifies against him, it moves from outside him to inside him, and it changes from a passing traveler to a guest to the master of the house. Feeding a desire only makes it hungrier. The יצר הרע is listed among four creations הקדוש ברוך הוא 'regrets,' and רבי יוחנן and רב פפא bring verses showing that ה׳ takes part in fixing the human heart. Next the גמרא identifies end-of-days figures: the four craftsmen in זכריה (after a challenge from רב ששת), and the seven shepherds and eight princes in מיכה. Finally it returns to the משנה of שמחת בית השואבה. It explains that the young כהנים carried 30 לוגין each up steep ladders, a feat greater than that of the strong son of מרתא בת בייתוס. It then begins a ברייתא about the light reaching every courtyard in ירושלים, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The evil inclination attacks daily, but God helps a person win
steps.stepSummary: This amud opens with the end of a verse about the יצר הרע thinking 'only evil all day.' Then ריש לקיש teaches that the יצר הרע overpowers a person every day and seeks to kill him. Without הקדוש ברוך הוא's help, a person could not beat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...evil all day.' רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: A person's inclination overpowers him every day and tries to kill him, as it says: 'The wicked one watches the righteous and seeks to kill him.' And if not for הקדוש ברוך הוא helping him, he could not beat it, as it says: 'ה׳ will not leave him in his hand, and will not let him be condemned when he is judged.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש makes a statement: the יצר הרע attacks a person every single day and tries to destroy him. Only הקדוש ברוך הוא's help lets the person survive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'the wicked one' in the verse as the יצר הרע and 'the righteous one' as the person it hunts. The very next verse says ה׳ will not abandon the righteous into the wicked one's hand, which shows that victory comes only with Divine help. The opening words 'רע כל היום' are the end of a verse (בראשית ו:ה) quoted at the end of the previous amud, which already showed that the יצר הרע is active all day.

keyTerms.meaning: His inclination; here the evil inclination (יצר הרע)

steps.confusionAlert: 'רע כל היום' is not the start of a new statement. It is the tail end of a verse quoted at the end of the previous section, so do not read it as part of ריש לקיש's words.

phrases.english: "...evil all day."
phrases.notes: End of the verse in בראשית ו:ה, carried over from the previous section.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: יִצְרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו בְּכׇל יוֹם
phrases.english: A person's inclination overpowers him every day
and seeks to kill him,
as it says: "The wicked one watches the righteous and seeks to kill him,"
phrases.notes: תהלים לז:לב. 'The wicked one' is read as the יצר הרע.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁעוֹזֵר לוֹ —
phrases.english: and if not for the Holy One, Blessed be He, who helps him,
he could not overcome it,
as it says: "ה׳ will not leave him in his hand,
phrases.notes: תהלים לז:לג, the very next verse.

phrases.english: and will not let him be condemned when he is judged."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier אגדה about the יצר הרע on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע attacks a person daily and seeks to kill him; only הקדוש ברוך הוא's help enables a person to overcome it.

steps.title: The cure: drag the evil inclination to the study hall
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that when the יצר הרע attacks you, you should pull it into the בית המדרש. תורה will either dissolve it, if it is like stone, or shatter it, if it is like iron.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: If this disgusting one (the יצר הרע) meets you, drag it to the בית המדרש. If it is stone, it will dissolve. If it is iron, it will shatter.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל gives practical advice: fight the יצר הרע by learning תורה. However tough it is, תורה will break it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After ריש לקיש said a person needs Divine help, this ברייתא shows the tool a person can use: תורה study. It describes two levels of hardness. Stone gets slowly worn away, and iron gets smashed. The verses proving both images come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
Disgusting one, scoundrel; a nickname for the יצר הרע

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the most famous sources for the idea that תורה study is the main weapon against the יצר הרע.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
If this scoundrel meets you,
phrases.notes: 'This scoundrel' means the יצר הרע.

phrases.english: drag it to the study hall.
If it is stone, it will dissolve;
if it is iron, it will shatter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing that a person needs help against the יצר הרע, we now learn the practical method: תורה study.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bring the יצר הרע into the בית המדרש; תורה dissolves it like stone or shatters it like iron.

steps.title: Verses proving that תורה dissolves stone and shatters iron
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats each half of the ברייתא and brings a verse for it. תורה is compared to water, and water wears away stone. תורה is also compared to fire and to a hammer that smashes rock.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If it is stone, it dissolves,' as it is written: 'Ho, everyone who is thirsty, come to the water,' and it is written: 'Water wears away stones.' 'If it is iron, it shatters,' as it is written: 'Is not My word like fire, says ה׳, and like a hammer that shatters rock?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the two images from the ברייתא and gives a scriptural source for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stone: the first verse (ישעיה נה:א) compares תורה to water, and the second (איוב יד:יט) says water wears down stones, so תורה wears down a stony יצר הרע. Iron: ירמיה כג:כט compares ה׳'s word to a hammer that breaks rock, so תורה shatters even an iron-hard יצר הרע. The repetition here is real, because the גמרא restates each phrase in order to attach a proof to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Thirsty; read as someone thirsting for תורה

steps.confusionAlert: The first proof needs two verses together. Neither verse alone proves the point: one says תורה is water, and the other says water wears down stone.
steps.whatToRemember: תורה is like water that slowly wears down a hard יצר הרע, and like a hammer that can smash even the toughest one.

phrases.english: "If it is stone, it will dissolve":
as it is written: "Ho, everyone who is thirsty, come to the water,"
phrases.notes: ישעיה נה:א. Water here means תורה.

phrases.english: and it is written: "Water wears away stones."
phrases.notes: איוב יד:יט

phrases.english: "If it is iron, it will shatter":

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״הֲלׂא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ נְאֻם ה׳
phrases.english: as it is written: "Is not My word like fire, says ה׳,
phrases.notes: ירמיה כג:כט

phrases.english: and like a hammer that shatters rock?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings verses to support each of the two images in the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's claim that תורה dissolves a stone-like יצר הרע and shatters an iron-like one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיה נה:א together with איוב יד:יט for stone; ירמיה כג:כט for iron.

steps.title: The evil inclination tempts now and testifies later
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני, in the name of רבי יונתן, teaches that the יצר הרע tempts a person in this world and then testifies against him in עולם הבא. He brings a verse from משלי ending with the word 'מנון.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: The יצר הרע tempts a person in this world and testifies against him in עולם הבא, as it says: 'One who pampers his servant from youth, in the end he will be a מנון.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: the same יצר הרע that pushes a person to sin later becomes the witness against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse (משלי כט:כא) describes someone who spoils his servant from youth. Here the 'servant' is the יצר הרע, which should have been under the person's control but was pampered instead. In the end it becomes a 'מנון.' The meaning of that unusual word is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Tempts him, entices him to sin

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:

phrases.aramaic: יֵצֶר הָרָע מְסִיתוֹ לָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
phrases.english: The evil inclination tempts a person in this world,
and testifies against him in the World to Come,
as it says: "One who pampers his servant from youth,
phrases.notes: משלי כט:כא

phrases.english: in the end he will be a 'manon.'"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new teaching about the יצר הרע: its role after death, not only during life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע entices a person in this world and then testifies against him in עולם הבא.

steps.title: A letter code shows that מנון means 'witness'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the word 'מנון' with רבי חייא's letter code, אטב״ח. In that code, the word סהדה ('witness') turns into מנון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because in the אטב״ח of רבי חייא, they call a witness (סהדה) 'מנון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the unusual word at the end of the verse, which proves that the verse is talking about a witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אטב״ח is a code that swaps letters in pairs, for example א↔ט and ב↔ח. In this code, ס becomes מ, ה becomes נ, and ד becomes ו. So סהדה, the Aramaic word for witness, becomes מנון. This completes the proof that the יצר הרע ends up as a witness.

keyTerms.meaning: A letter-substitution code that swaps letters in pairs (א↔ט, ב↔ח, and so on)
The coded form of סהדה, meaning witness

steps.confusionAlert: 'מנון' is not a normal Hebrew word here. You only get 'witness' by decoding it with אטב״ח.
steps.whatToRemember: The יצר הרע plays both sides: it pushes a person to sin and then testifies against him.

phrases.english: for in the atbach code of Rabbi Chiya,
they call a witness (sahada) 'manon.'
phrases.notes: The code swaps each letter: ס becomes מ, ה becomes נ, ד becomes ו, and the last ה becomes ן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the key word in the verse just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: That 'מנון' in משלי כט:כא means witness.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's אטב״ח letter code, which turns סהדה into מנון.

steps.title: Two verses disagree about where the spirit of promiscuity is
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא points out a contradiction. One verse says the spirit of זנונים 'led them astray,' as if it comes from outside. Another verse says it is 'inside them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא raised a contradiction: It is written, 'For a spirit of זנונים led them astray,' and it is written, 'within them'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא sets two verses side by side that seem to clash. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הושע ד:יב says the spirit 'led them astray,' which sounds like an outside force acting on them. הושע ה:ד says the spirit is 'בקרבם,' within them, which sounds like part of who they are. So which is it: outside or inside?

keyTerms.meaning: Raised a contradiction, set verses against each other
Spirit of promiscuity; the urge to sin

phrases.english: Rav Huna raised a contradiction:
It is written: "For a spirit of promiscuity led them astray,"
phrases.notes: הושע ד:יב

phrases.english: and it is written: "within them"!
phrases.notes: הושע ה:ד: "for a spirit of promiscuity is within them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about the יצר הרע, opened by a contradiction between verses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two verses in הושע describing the spirit of זנונים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One verse places the spirit outside the person, acting on him. The other places it inside him, as part of him.

steps.title: First it leads astray from outside, later it lives inside
steps.stepSummary: The answer: at first the urge to sin only misleads a person from the outside, but in the end it settles inside him.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first it leads them astray, and in the end it is within them.
steps.whatsHappening: The contradiction is resolved by explaining that the two verses describe two stages of sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each verse describes a different stage. When a person first sins, the urge is still a visitor that 'leads him astray.' If he keeps giving in, it becomes part of him, 'within them.' So both verses are true, at different times.
steps.whatToRemember: Sin starts as an outside pull, but repeated giving in makes it part of the person.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that it is easiest to resist the יצר הרע early, before it becomes part of a person.

phrases.english: At first it leads them astray,
and in the end it is within them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רב הונא's contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Time-stage distinction: each verse describes a different stage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verses seem to disagree about whether the spirit of זנונים is outside or inside a person.
steps.terutzMaskana: First it misleads from outside; after repeated sin it lives within the person.

steps.title: רבא: The evil urge goes from traveler to guest to master
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that the פסוק first calls the יצר הרע a 'traveler,' then a 'guest,' and finally 'a man.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: At first the פסוק called it a 'traveler,' later it called it a 'guest,' and in the end it called it 'a man.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new teaching about how the יצר הרע slowly takes over a person. It moves in three stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the last step, which said the urge starts outside a person and ends up inside him. רבא breaks that process into three names. A traveler is just passing by. A guest has been invited in. 'A man' is treated like the one who runs the house.

keyTerms.meaning: A traveler, someone just passing through
A guest, someone who has been welcomed in
A man; here it means someone important who is in charge

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that sin does not take over all at once. Each small welcome gives the יצר הרע more power.

phrases.english: Rava said:
At first [the verse] called it a "traveler,"
phrases.notes: Someone passing by who does not stay.

phrases.english: and later it called it a "guest,"
phrases.notes: Now it has been invited in.

phrases.english: and in the end it called it a "man,"
phrases.notes: Now it acts like the owner of the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 7's 'outside first, then inside' into a three-stage process.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע grows step by step: traveler, then guest, then master.

steps.title: The proof from נתן's parable of the poor man's lamb
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the פסוק from נתן הנביא's parable to דוד, where all three words (הלך, אורח, איש) appear in order.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'A traveler came to the rich man, and he did not want to take from his own sheep and cattle to prepare for the guest.' And it is written: 'He took the poor man's lamb and prepared it for the man who came to him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his three stages from one פסוק in שמואל ב. The same visitor is first called הלך, then אורח, then איש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the parable, one visitor gets three different names in a single story. רבא reads this as a picture of the יצר הרע gaining importance. The story is about דוד's sin, so it fits a lesson about how desire takes over.

keyTerms.meaning: And he spared (did not want to use his own)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think these are three different visitors. It is one visitor with three names. That is exactly רבא's point.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "And a traveler came to the rich man,"
and he did not want to take from his own flock and his own herd
to prepare for the guest"
phrases.notes: Second name: guest.

phrases.english: And it is written: "And he took the poor man's lamb
and prepared it for the man who had come to him."
phrases.notes: Third name: man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוק that proves רבא's statement in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's three stages of the יצר הרע
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב יב:ד, the parable of the poor man's lamb

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Feeding a desire makes it hungrier
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that a person has a small organ that stays satisfied when it is starved and gets hungrier when it is fed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A person has a small organ. If he starves it, it is satisfied. If he feeds it, it is hungry. As it says: 'When they were fed, they became full...' (and then they forgot Me).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds another lesson about desire. Giving in to it does not calm it down; it makes it want more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, eating ends hunger. רבי יוחנן says physical desire works the opposite way. Holding back keeps it calm, and indulging makes the craving stronger. The פסוק in הושע shows that being 'filled' led the people to pride and to forgetting הקדוש ברוך הוא.

keyTerms.meaning: A small organ (a modest way to refer to the organ of physical desire)

steps.confusionAlert: The two halves sound backwards, and that is on purpose. Starving it leads to 'full,' and feeding it leads to 'hungry.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
A person has a small organ:
if he starves it, it is satisfied;
if he feeds it, it is hungry,
as it is stated: "When they were fed, they became full, etc."
phrases.notes: הושע יג:ו. The verse goes on: 'their heart became proud, so they forgot Me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵבֶר קָטָן יֵשׁ לוֹ לָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new teaching about the יצר הרע: indulging it makes it stronger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holding back from desire calms it, and indulging it increases it.

steps.title: Four creations that God 'regrets' creating
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר אחא, quoting the school of רב, lists four things הקדוש ברוך הוא 'regrets' creating: גלות, כשדים, ישמעאלים, and the יצר הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר אחא said that they say in the school of רב: There are four things that הקדוש ברוך הוא regrets creating. They are: exile, the Chaldeans, the Ishmaelites, and the evil urge.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement gives a list of four things. It sets up the next step, where the גמרא brings a פסוק for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list ends with the יצר הרע, which ties it to the whole discussion. 'Regret' here is a figure of speech: these creations cause much harm to כלל ישראל. The other three are outside enemies and troubles, and the יצר הרע is the enemy inside.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as if הקדוש ברוך הוא made a mistake. The language of 'regret' is a way of saying how much harm these things cause.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר אַחָא, אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Acha said: They say in the school of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה מִתְחָרֵט עֲלֵיהֶן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁבְּרָאָם,
phrases.english: There are four things the Holy One, Blessed be He, regrets having created,
and these are they: exile, the Chaldeans,
and the Ishmaelites, and the evil urge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר אַחָא, אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב: אַרְבָּעָה מִתְחָרֵט עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement whose list ends with the יצר הרע, continuing the theme.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four creations are described as 'regretted' by הקדוש ברוך הוא: גלות, כשדים, ישמעאלים, and the יצר הרע.

steps.title: A verse for each of the four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק to show each of the four items: גלות, כשדים, ישמעאלים, and the יצר הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Exile, as it is written: 'Now what do I have here, says ה׳, since My people were taken for nothing...' The Chaldeans, as it is written: 'Behold the land of the Chaldeans; this people was not.' The Ishmaelites, as it is written: 'The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who anger God are secure, to whom God brought with His hand.' The evil urge, as it is written: 'And whom I have done harm.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now proves each item on the list with a פסוק, one by one. Each פסוק hints that הקדוש ברוך הוא is, so to speak, unhappy with that creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For גלות‎, ה׳ asks 'what do I have here?', as if the exile troubles Him. For כשדים, 'this people was not' is read as 'if only they had never been.' For ישמעאלים, the robbers in tents are ones 'God brought with His hand.' For the יצר הרע, 'whom I have done harm' shows that ה׳ takes responsibility for creating the thing that leads people to sin.
steps.whatToRemember: The יצר הרע starts as a passing traveler and can become the master of the house. Indulging it makes it stronger. It is so harmful that חז״ל list it with גלות and Israel's enemies as creations הקדוש ברוך הוא 'regrets.'

phrases.english: Exile, as it is written:
"And now, what do I have here, says the Lord,
phrases.notes: ישעיה נב:ה‎. ה׳ Himself asks this, as if the exile troubles Him.

phrases.english: since My people was taken away for nothing, etc."
The Chaldeans, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״הֵן אֶרֶץ כַּשְׂדִּים זֶה הָעָם לֹא הָיָה״.
phrases.english: "Behold the land of the Chaldeans; this people was not."
phrases.notes: ישעיה כג:יג. Read as: if only they had never existed.

phrases.english: The Ishmaelites, as it is written:
"The tents of robbers are at peace,
phrases.notes: איוב יב:ו. Desert tribes living in tents.

phrases.english: and those who anger God are secure,
those whom God brought with His hand."
The evil urge, as it is written: "And whom I have done harm."
phrases.notes: מיכה ד:ו‎. ה׳ says He created the thing that caused them harm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves each of the four items listed in step 11 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיה נב:ה, ישעיה כג:יג, איוב יב:ו, מיכה ד:ו

steps.title: Three verses that keep Israel from falling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that without three specific פסוקים, the Jewish people would have collapsed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If not for these three verses, the legs of 'the enemies of Israel' (a polite way of saying Israel itself) would have given way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן makes a new statement: three פסוקים are what keep the Jewish people standing. The next step will list the three פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on Step 11, where הקדוש ברוך הוא 'regrets' creating the יצר הרע. If ה׳ admits He made the יצר הרע and promises to take it away, then Israel's sins are not judged with full harshness. Without that, Israel could not survive the weight of its sins. The phrase 'enemies of Israel' is a softer way of saying 'Israel.' The גמרא does not want to say directly that harm would come to Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The enemies of Israel.' A polite way to refer to Israel itself

steps.confusionAlert: 'The enemies of Israel' does NOT mean Israel's actual enemies here. It is a softened way of saying 'Israel.' The גמרא avoids writing something bad directly about the Jewish people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Were it not for these three verses,
the legs would have collapsed
of the 'enemies' of Israel (i.e., Israel itself).
phrases.notes: A polite way of speaking, so the גמרא does not say something bad directly about Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִלְמָלֵא שָׁלֹשׁ מִקְרָאוֹת הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of ה׳ 'regretting' the יצר הרע and shows why that matters for Israel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three פסוקים showing ה׳'s role in the יצר הרע are what keep Israel from collapsing under its sins.

steps.title: Listing the three verses
steps.stepSummary: The three פסוקים are quoted: 'ואשר הרעתי,' 'like clay in the potter's hand,' and 'I will remove the heart of stone.'
steps.simpleTranslation: One verse is 'And her that I made bad.' Another is 'Behold, like clay in the potter's hand, so are you…' The other is 'I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists the three פסוקים that רבי יוחנן was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק shows that ה׳ has a hand in the human heart. In 'ואשר הרעתי‎,' ה׳ says He caused the harm. In the clay image, people are shaped by the Potter. In the third פסוק‎, ה׳ Himself promises to replace the stony heart, meaning the יצר הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And her that I made bad.' ה׳ takes responsibility (מיכה)
Heart of stone, meaning the יצר הרע (יחזקאל)

phrases.english: One, as it is written: "And her that I have harmed."
And one, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״הִנֵּה כַחוֹמֶר בְּיַד הַיּוֹצֵר כֵּן אַתֶּם וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "Behold, like clay in the potter's hand, so are you, etc."
And the other:
"And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh
and I will give you a heart of flesh."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the three פסוקים that רבי יוחנן referred to.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that three פסוקים protect Israel
steps.raayaSupportSource: מיכה ד:ו, ירמיה יח:ו, יחזקאל לו:כו

steps.title: רב פפא adds a fourth verse
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the same idea can also be learned from 'ואת רוחי אתן בקרבכם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Also from this verse: "And I will put My spirit within you, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds another פסוק that teaches the same idea as רבי יוחנן's three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next פסוק in יחזקאל says ה׳ will put His spirit inside us and cause us to follow His laws. This shows even more clearly that ה׳ helps people do good. So רב פפא counts it as one more source of protection for Israel.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר, אַף מֵהַאי נָמֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: also from this one too:
"And I will put My spirit within you, etc."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל לו:כז. It continues 'and I will cause you to walk in My laws.'

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן and רב פפא teach that ה׳ admits His role in creating the יצר הרע and promises to remove it. This is what lets Israel survive its sins.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר, אַף מֵהַאי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth פסוק to רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that ה׳ controls the heart and will fix it

steps.title: Who are the four craftsmen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes זכריה's vision of 'four craftsmen' and asks who they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And ה׳ showed me four craftsmen." Who are these four craftsmen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about the end of days. It quotes a פסוק and asks what it means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the talk was about the final redemption, when the יצר הרע will be removed, the גמרא moves to another vision of the future. In זכריה's vision, four 'horns' scatter Judah and four 'craftsmen' come. The גמרא wants to know who these craftsmen are.

phrases.english: "And the Lord showed me four craftsmen"
phrases.notes: זכריה ב:ג

phrases.english: Who are these four craftsmen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new end-of-days topic, connected by the theme of the future redemption.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the four craftsmen in זכריה's vision.

steps.title: The four craftsmen are four redeemers
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר ביזנא, quoting רבי שמעון חסידא, says the four are משיח בן דוד, משיח בן יוסף, אליהו, and כהן צדק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר ביזנא said in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא: they are משיח בן דוד, משיח בן יוסף, אליהו, and the righteous כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the four craftsmen are four figures who will bring the redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These four craftsmen are the good figures of the future who will come and fix the world. משיח בן יוסף (from earlier in this סוגיא) is listed together with משיח בן דוד, אליהו, and a righteous כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: משיח descended from דוד, the final redeemer
משיח descended from יוסף, who comes earlier
אליהו the prophet, who announces the redemption
The righteous כהן (a כהן גדול of the future)

phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Bizna said
that Rabbi Shimon Chasida said:

phrases.aramaic: מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד, וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: Mashiach ben David, and Mashiach ben Yosef,
and Eliyahu, and the righteous Kohen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר בִּיזְנָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן חֲסִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of who the four craftsmen are.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The four craftsmen are משיח בן דוד, משיח בן יוסף, אליהו, and כהן צדק.

steps.title: רב ששת: the verse calls them destroyers
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת challenges: when the נביא asks what the craftsmen come to do, the answer speaks of 'the horns that scattered Judah.' But משיח, אליהו and the others come for good, so why are they tied to the scattering of Judah?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: If so, look at what is written: "And he said to me: These are the horns that scattered Judah." But these (משיח, אליהו, etc.) come for good!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks the answer. He reads the next פסוק as describing the four as harmful forces against Judah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת reads the angel's reply ('these are the horns that scattered Judah') as describing the four craftsmen's mission. But the four figures רבי שמעון חסידא named come for good (לשובה), not to scatter Judah. So the identification looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Horns, a symbol of the nations' power

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objected:
If so, what about that which is written:
"And he said to me: These are the horns
that scattered Judah"
But these (righteous figures) come for good!
phrases.notes: לשובה means 'for good.' But when the verse answers 'what do these come to do?', it talks about the horns that scattered Judah, which doesn't fit righteous redeemers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the four craftsmen are four redeemers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The next פסוק seems to call 'these' the horns that scattered Judah. That describes destroyers, not redeemers.

steps.title: Look at the end of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא answers: the end of the פסוק shows the craftsmen come to cast down the horns of the nations. So the horns and the craftsmen are different groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Look at the end of the verse: "And these came to frighten them, to cast down the horns of the nations who raised a horn against the land of Judah to scatter it, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנא defends his answer. He tells רב ששת to read the rest of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק separates the two groups. The 'horns' are the nations that scattered Judah. The craftsmen come to frighten those nations and knock down their horns. So the craftsmen are the saviors who defeat the enemies, just as רב חנא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Go down to the end of the verse

phrases.english: He said to him: go down to the end of the verse:
"And these came to frighten them,
to cast down the horns of the nations
who raise a horn against the land of Judah
to scatter it, etc."

steps.confusionAlert: There are two groups in זכריה's vision: the four horns (the enemy nations) and the four craftsmen (the redeemers). רב ששת's question mixed them up. The end of the פסוק separates them.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the full פסוק in context
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת thought the four craftsmen were the horns that scattered Judah.
steps.terutzMaskana: The horns are the enemy nations. The craftsmen come to destroy those horns, so they are redeemers.

steps.title: רב ששת yields to רב חנא in אגדתא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת gives in, saying: why should I argue with רב חנא in אגדתא?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why do I need to get into it with חנא in matters of אגדתא?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת accepts the answer. He admits that רב חנא is the expert in אגדתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת does not push his challenge further. He recognizes that רב חנא knows this area better. So the identification of the four craftsmen as four redeemers stands.

keyTerms.meaning: אגדה, the non-legal teachings of חז״ל

steps.whatToRemember: The four craftsmen in זכריה are משיח בן דוד, משיח בן יוסף, אליהו, and כהן צדק. They come to knock down the 'horns' (the enemy nations) that scattered Judah.

phrases.english: He (Rav Sheshet) said to him:
Why should I take on Chana in Aggadah?
phrases.notes: רב חנא was known as an expert in Aggadah, so רב ששת gives in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ששת accepts the answer from Step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב ששת withdraws his objection. The four craftsmen are the four redeemers, as רבי שמעון חסידא said.

steps.title: Who are the seven shepherds in Micah's vision?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק in מיכה about seven shepherds and eight princes who will rise against Assyria, and asks who the seven shepherds are.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And this shall be peace: when Assyria comes into our land and treads in our palaces, we will raise against him seven shepherds and eight princes of men.' Who are the 'seven shepherds'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more end-of-days פסוק and asks who the 'seven shepherds' are. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the pattern from the 'four craftsmen': a פסוק names a group of future saviors without saying who they are. The גמרא now wants their identities. The first question is only about the seven shepherds.

keyTerms.meaning: Seven shepherds (leaders who guide and protect the people)
Eight princes of men (eight great leaders)
Assyria, the enemy in the פסוק

phrases.english: "And this shall be peace:
phrases.notes: מיכה ה:ד

phrases.english: when Assyria comes into our land
and when he treads in our palaces,
then we will raise up against him seven shepherds
and eight princes of men."
Who are the "seven shepherds"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'four craftsmen' discussion ends, the גמרא moves to a similar end-of-days פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identities of the seven shepherds in the פסוק in מיכה.

steps.title: The seven shepherds, with David in the middle
steps.stepSummary: דוד stands in the middle. אדם, שת, and מתושלח are on his right, and אברהם, יעקב, and משה are on his left.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד is in the middle. אדם, שת, and מתושלח are on his right. אברהם, יעקב, and משה are on his left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by naming the seven shepherds. It also places them around דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are seven people: דוד plus three on each side. Putting דוד in the center fits the idea that the final redemption comes through the house of דוד. Great figures from before the מבול (אדם, שת, מתושלח) stand on one side, and אברהם, יעקב, and משה stand on the other.

phrases.english: David is in the middle;
Adam, Seth, and Methuselah are to his right;
Abraham, Jacob, and Moses are to his left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דוד in the center, with אדם, שת, and מתושלח on his right and אברהם, יעקב, and משה on his left.

steps.title: Who are the eight princes of men?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks about the second group in the פסוק: the eight princes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who are the 'eight princes of men'?
steps.whatsHappening: Having named the seven shepherds, the גמרא asks about the eight princes. This sets up the list that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the second half of the same פסוק. The question has the same form as the one about the seven shepherds.

phrases.english: And who are the "eight princes of men"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first group in the פסוק to the second.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identities of the eight princes.

steps.title: The list of the eight princes
steps.stepSummary: The eight princes are ישי, שאול, שמואל, עמוס, צפניה, צדקיה, משיח, and אליהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישי, שאול, שמואל, עמוס, צפניה, צדקיה, משיח, and אליהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists the eight princes. This finishes the end-of-days אגדתא section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list mixes kings, prophets, and figures of the future redemption. It ends with משיח and אליהו, who also appeared among the 'four craftsmen.'

keyTerms.meaning: Elijah the prophet, who announces the redemption

steps.whatToRemember: This אגדתא closes by naming the 'seven shepherds' (with דוד in the middle) and the 'eight princes' (ending with משיח and אליהו). Next, the גמרא goes back to the משנה about שמחת בית השואבה.

phrases.english: Jesse, and Saul, and Samuel,
Amos, and Zephaniah, Zedekiah,
and Messiah, and Elijah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23 and closes the אגדתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ישי, שאול, שמואל, עמוס, צפניה, צדקיה, משיח, and אליהו.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the lamp height and the oil jugs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'four ladders' and brings a ברייתא: the lamp-stand was 50 אמות tall, and four young כהנים carried jugs holding 120 לוגין of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'four ladders' and so on. A ברייתא taught: the lamp-stand was fifty cubits tall. Four boys from the young כהנים held jugs of oil of one hundred twenty לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the אגדתא and returns to the משנה about the ladders used to fill the lamps at שמחת בית השואבה. It adds details from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds two facts the משנה did not give: how tall the lamp-stand was and how much oil the boys carried. The phrase '120 לוגין' is unclear, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid measure (about the volume of six eggs)

phrases.english: Four ladders, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: גּוֹבְהָהּ שֶׁל מְנוֹרָה חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה,
phrases.english: It was taught: The height of the lamp-stand was fifty cubits,
and four children from the young priest-trainees,
and in their hands were jugs of oil
of one hundred twenty log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדתא and returns to explaining the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lamp-stand was 50 אמות high, and four young כהנים carried jugs holding 120 לוגין of oil.

steps.title: Was the 120 לוגין the total or per boy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the 120 לוגין was the total for all four boys or the amount each boy carried.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: was it 120 לוגין for all of them together, or perhaps 120 for each one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the wording of the ברייתא. Does '120 לוגין' describe all four boys together or each boy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's wording can be read both ways. If it means each boy, then 480 לוגין were carried in all, which is a big difference.

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
was it one hundred twenty log for all of them together,
or perhaps for each and every one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ברייתא in step 25 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 120 לוגין is the total amount or the amount for each boy.

steps.title: Proof: 30 each, 120 in total
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says each jug held 30 לוגין, which adds up to 120 in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: in their hands were jugs of oil of thirty לוגין each, which all together come to 120 לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question by quoting a ברייתא that spells it out clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'thirty thirty' (thirty each) and 'all of them together are 120' settle it. 120 is the total, so each boy carried 30.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is coming)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
and in their hands were jugs of oil
of thirty log each,
which all together are one hundred twenty log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 26 with a clearer ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 120 לוגין was the total, with 30 per boy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating 30 לוגין each, 120 in total.

steps.title: The young כהנים were more impressive than a famous strongman
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא praises these boys as more impressive than the son of מרתא בת בייתוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: these boys were more praiseworthy than the son of מרתא בת בייתוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא praises the young כהנים by comparing them to a famously strong כהן. The next step will explain who he was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new claim: the boys' feat was greater than a well-known feat of strength. It sets up the story that follows and the question that comes after it.

keyTerms.meaning: A wealthy woman from a priestly family; her son was famous for his strength

phrases.english: It was taught: And they were more praiseworthy

phrases.aramaic: יוֹתֵר מִבְּנָהּ שֶׁל מָרְתָּא בַּת בַּיְיתּוֹס.
phrases.english: than the son of Marta, daughter of Baitos.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds praise for the boys who carried the oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oil-carrying boys were more impressive than the son of מרתא בת בייתוס.

steps.title: The strength of the son of מרתא בת בייתוס
steps.stepSummary: He could carry two thighs of a huge, costly ox and walk slowly, heel to toe. The other כהנים stopped him, because of 'ברב עם הדרת מלך.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about him that he would take both thighs of a huge ox bought for a thousand זוז and walk heel to toe, in tiny calm steps. His fellow כהנים did not let him do this, because 'In the multitude of people is the King's glory.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא describes the famous strongman so we can see how impressive the boys were. It also notes that his fellow כהנים would not let him do this job alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking heel to toe shows he was not straining at all under a very heavy load. The other כהנים stopped him because the עבודה brings more honor to the King when many people share in it.

keyTerms.meaning: Heel next to toe, meaning tiny, calm steps
In a multitude of people is the King's glory

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'ברב עם הדרת מלך' is used across ש״ס. It teaches that a מצוה done by many people together gives more honor to ה׳.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עַל בְּנָהּ שֶׁל מָרְתָּא בַּת בַּיְיתּוֹס
phrases.english: They said about the son of Marta, daughter of Baitos,
that he would take two thighs
of a large ox
that was bought for a thousand zuz,
and walk heel beside toe.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הֱנִיחוּהוּ אֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן,
phrases.english: But his brothers the priests did not let him do so,
because of: "In the multitude of people is the King's glory."
phrases.notes: משלי יד:כח

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עַל בְּנָהּ שֶׁל מָרְתָּא בַּת בַּיְיתּוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains who the comparison figure from step 28 was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He carried two huge ox thighs with ease, but the כהנים stopped him because of 'ברב עם הדרת מלך.'

steps.title: In what way were the boys more impressive?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what made the boys more impressive than the strongman.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what way were they more praiseworthy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by 'more praiseworthy.' This sets up a suggested answer, a rejection of it, and a final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison is not obvious, so the גמרא wants to know exactly what was greater about the boys' feat.

phrases.english: In what way were they more praiseworthy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the comparison made in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made the boys more impressive.

steps.title: It can't be about weight
steps.stepSummary: If the point were weight, that cannot be right, because two ox thighs are heavier than 30 לוגין of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was because of the weight, but these thighs are heavier!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible answer, that the boys carried more weight, and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each boy carried only 30 לוגין. Two thighs of a giant ox weigh much more than that. So weight cannot explain why the boys were 'more praiseworthy.'

phrases.english: If you say it is because of the weight —
these (thighs) are heavier!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests and rejects one answer to step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects weight as the reason for the comparison.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ox thighs weighed more than 30 לוגין of oil.

steps.title: The difference: a gentle ramp vs. steep ladders
steps.stepSummary: He walked up the broad, gently sloped ramp of the מזבח. The boys climbed very steep ladders.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: there, it was the ramp, which was broad and not steep. Here, it was ladders, which are very steep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason the boys were more impressive. It was not the weight but the steep climb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כבש (ramp of the מזבח) was wide with a gentle slope, so carrying a load up it is easier. The boys climbed straight-up ladders to a 50-אמה height while holding full jugs, which is a much harder feat.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Broad, or sloping gently (one rise per four lengths)

steps.whatToRemember: Each boy carried 30 לוגין (120 in total). They were praised above the son of מרתא בת בייתוס not for carrying more weight, but because they climbed steep ladders, while he walked up a gentle ramp.

phrases.english: Rather: there it was the ramp,
and it was broad and gentle, and not steep.
phrases.notes: Read either as wide, or as a slope of one אמה up for every four forward

phrases.english: Here it was ladders, and very steep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected weight answer with the correct one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different point of comparison (how steep the climb was, not how heavy the load was).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the praise was about carrying heavier loads.
steps.terutzMaskana: The praise is about climbing steep ladders compared with a gentle ramp.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The young כהנים were more impressive because of how hard and steep their climb was, not because of how much they carried.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: no courtyard was left without light
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה about the light of בית השואבה reaching every courtyard in ירושלים. It then says תנא to introduce a ברייתא about that phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And there was not a courtyard in ירושלים' that was not lit up by the light of בית השואבה. A ברייתא teaches:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story of the strong כהן and returns to the משנה, quoting its next line. It then says תנא, which sets up a ברייתא that comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the light of the celebration was so strong that every courtyard in ירושלים was lit. The word תנא tells us a ברייתא is coming to show how strong that light really was. This line itself is only an opening; the explanation comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A courtyard, the open area shared by the houses around it
Jerusalem, the city of the בית המקדש
'It was taught.' This word introduces a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
The place of the water-drawing. Its huge torches lit up the city during סוכות

steps.confusionAlert: Only the first words of the משנה are quoted here. The full line says no courtyard in ירושלים was left unlit by the light of בית השואבה. Also, the word תנא does not end anything. The ברייתא it introduces comes in the next part of the text.

phrases.english: "And there was not a courtyard in Jerusalem" (that was not lit by the light of the water-drawing celebration).
phrases.notes: These are the first words of the next line of the משנה.

phrases.english: It was taught (in a ברייתא):
phrases.notes: This ברייתא explains the משנה's line; what it says comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of the boys and the strongman (steps 28-32). It goes back to the משנה and starts a new topic: how bright the light of בית השואבה was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's claim that every courtyard in ירושלים was lit is about to be explained by a ברייתא.
